sections.title: Stoics
sections.blurb: From the Roman practice to the modern Stoic books. Ancient texts can be read in public-domain English. The new books stay cards.

sections.title: Robert Greene
sections.blurb: One card for each real book. The shelf does not copy a law, a story, or a page.

sections.title: Scripture
sections.blurb: A broad scripture room in the spirit of a Vatican hall or the Cayce library. These cards name canons. They are not those buildings, and they do not paste chapters.

sections.title: Metaphysical and ancient gods
sections.blurb: Hermetica, Kabbalah, and books of the old gods. Atlantis enters through Plato. Later Atlantis books are marked as claims.

volumes.author: Marcus Aurelius
volumes.note: A Roman emperor's private notebook of Stoic practice.

volumes.author: Seneca
volumes.note: Moral letters from the end of Seneca's life.

volumes.author: Seneca
volumes.note: A short essay on how people spend the time they already have.

volumes.author: Seneca
volumes.note: Three books on what anger does and how a person meets it.

volumes.author: Epictetus, recorded by Arrian
volumes.note: Classroom talks on what is up to us and what is not.

volumes.author: Epictetus, compiled by Arrian
volumes.note: A short handbook drawn from the Discourses.

volumes.author: Musonius Rufus
volumes.note: Notes from the teacher of Epictetus, kept by a student.

volumes.author: Ryan Holiday
volumes.note: A modern Stoic book on using difficulty as the work.

volumes.author: Ryan Holiday
volumes.note: A modern book on ego before, during, and after a success.

volumes.author: Ryan Holiday and Stephen Hanselman
volumes.note: A daybook that points at old Stoic passages.

volumes.author: Ryan Holiday
volumes.note: A modern book on quiet as a working discipline.

volumes.author: Ryan Holiday and Stephen Hanselman
volumes.note: Short lives of Stoic figures, written for current readers.

volumes.author: Ryan Holiday
volumes.note: A modern book on self-command as the Stoic virtue.

volumes.author: Ryan Holiday
volumes.note: A modern book treating fear and valor through historical examples.

volumes.author: Ryan Holiday
volumes.note: A modern book examining justice and moral duty as daily practice.

volumes.volume: A Guide to the Good Life
volumes.author: William B. Irvine
volumes.note: An introduction translating Roman Stoic techniques for contemporary living.

volumes.volume: How to Think Like a Roman Emperor
volumes.author: Donald Robertson
volumes.note: A study integrating Marcus Aurelius's life with cognitive behavioral practice.

volumes.author: Pierre Hadot
volumes.note: A philosophical monograph uncovering the spiritual exercises inside Marcus Aurelius's Meditations.

volumes.author: Massimo Pigliucci
volumes.note: A contemporary philosopher uses Epictetus as an informal guide through modern life.

volumes.author: Lawrence C. Becker
volumes.note: A rigorous philosophical revision asking what Stoic ethics would look like under modern science and logic.

volumes.author: Ward Farnsworth
volumes.note: A thematic arrangement of ancient Stoic thought grouped by core psychological subjects.

volumes.author: Robert Greene
volumes.note: Greene's first strategy book. The shelf keeps the title, not the laws.

volumes.author: Robert Greene
volumes.note: A book on persuasion and attraction. The card does not retell its stories.

volumes.author: Robert Greene
volumes.note: A strategy book that borrows the language of conflict for ordinary contests.

volumes.author: Robert Greene and 50 Cent
volumes.note: A joint book on fearlessness. It stays a card.

volumes.author: Robert Greene
volumes.note: Greene's book on a long apprenticeship. The shelf does not copy its chapters.

volumes.author: Robert Greene
volumes.note: A later Greene book on motives and character.

volumes.author: Robert Greene
volumes.note: A daybook drawn from Greene's earlier work.

volumes.author: Hebrew Bible
volumes.note: The Hebrew Bible: Torah, Prophets, and Writings. English translations differ in copyright.

volumes.author: Christian canon
volumes.note: The twenty-seven books common to the major Christian churches. The King James text is public domain. Many newer translations are not.

volumes.author: Catholic and Orthodox canons
volumes.note: Books kept by Catholic and Orthodox Bibles and set aside by most Protestant ones.

volumes.author: Islamic scripture
volumes.note: The Quran in Arabic is the scripture. English versions differ, and many translations are still in copyright.

volumes.author: Enochic collection
volumes.note: The Book of Enoch kept in the Ethiopian biblical tradition and found in fragments at Qumran. R. H. Charles's 1917 English is public domain.

volumes.author: Second Temple tradition
volumes.note: A retelling of Genesis and Exodus that counts time in jubilees.

volumes.author: Nag Hammadi collection
volumes.note: A sayings gospel found at Nag Hammadi. It is not in the New Testament canon.

volumes.author: Mahabharata
volumes.note: The conversation of Krishna and Arjuna inside the Mahabharata. Older English translations are public domain.

volumes.author: Pali canon
volumes.note: A short collection of verses from the Pali Buddhist canon.

volumes.author: attributed to Laozi
volumes.note: The short Daoist classic. Its date is disputed. Older English translations are public domain.

volumes.author: Muhammad al-Bukhari
volumes.note: A major Sunni collection of hadith. The shelf names it and does not quote it.

volumes.author: Vedic tradition
volumes.note: The foundational collection of Vedic hymns preserved through strict oral transmission before being committed to text.

volumes.author: Vedic sages
volumes.note: Early philosophical dialogues exploring Brahman and Atman at the conclusion of the Vedic corpus.

volumes.author: Zoroastrian tradition
volumes.note: The primary collection of sacred texts of Zoroastrianism, containing the Gathas attributed to Zarathustra.

volumes.author: Sikh Gurus and other contributors
volumes.note: The central religious scripture of Sikhism, regarded by Sikhs as the final sovereign and eternal living Guru.

volumes.author: Judah ha-Nasi and the Tannaim
volumes.note: The first major written redaction of the Jewish oral traditions known as the Oral Torah.

volumes.author: Rav Ashi, Ravina, and the Amoraim
volumes.note: The comprehensive compilation of rabbinic analysis, debates, and rulings on the Mishnah spanning generations.

volumes.author: Apostolic Fathers
volumes.note: A brief early Christian treatise containing instructions for Christian communities on morals, baptism, and church order.

volumes.author: Mahayana tradition
volumes.note: One of the most influential and venerated scriptures of East Asian Mahayana Buddhism on universal liberation.

volumes.author: Prajnaparamita tradition
volumes.note: A concise discourse encapsulating the Prajnaparamita doctrine on the fundamental emptiness of all phenomena.

volumes.author: attributed to Zhuang Zhou
volumes.note: The foundational Daoist text composed of parables and allegories questioning rigid conventional distinctions.

volumes.author: followers of Confucius
volumes.note: A collection of sayings and ideas attributed to Confucius and his contemporaries on virtue, ritual, and governance.

volumes.author: Mandaean tradition
volumes.note: The Great Treasure, serving as the central holy book and primary theological scripture of surviving Mandaeism.

volumes.author: Baha'u'llah
volumes.note: The central book of the Baha'i faith detailing its laws and ordinances; modern editions are kept in copyright.

volumes.author: Jain tradition
volumes.note: The first of the twelve Agamas containing the primary monastic conduct rules and ascetical life of Mahavira.

volumes.author: Plato
volumes.note: Plato's dialogue that tells the Atlantis story as a tale inside the dialogue.

volumes.author: Plato
volumes.note: The unfinished companion to Timaeus. This is the ancient Atlantis text, and it is Plato's story.

volumes.author: Hesiod
volumes.note: A Greek account of the birth of the gods.

volumes.author: Lucretius
volumes.note: A Latin poem that says the gods do not run the world. It sits here as an old book outside the temple.

volumes.author: Babylonian tradition
volumes.note: The Babylonian creation epic of Marduk and Tiamat.

volumes.author: ancient Egyptian tradition
volumes.note: A collection of Egyptian funerary spells. Older scholarly English is public domain.

volumes.author: K'iche' Maya
volumes.note: The K'iche' book of origins, set down after the Spanish invasion from an older tradition.

volumes.author: medieval Icelandic collection
volumes.note: The main medieval collection of Norse mythological poems.

volumes.author: attributed to Hermes Trismegistus
volumes.note: Greek philosophical texts under the name of Hermes, written in the Roman period, not a recovered Egyptian bible.

volumes.author: attributed to Hermes
volumes.note: A short medieval text later attached to Hermes. It is not an excavated Atlantean tablet.

volumes.author: Jewish mystical tradition
volumes.note: An early Jewish book on creation through letters and numbers. Its exact date is debated.

volumes.author: attributed to Shimon bar Yochai, associated with Moses de León
volumes.note: The central book of Kabbalah. The shelf names it. Modern translations stay off the card.

volumes.author: Augustine of Hippo
volumes.note: Augustine's account of a life turned toward God. A church father, not a hidden canon.

volumes.author: Boethius
volumes.note: A prison book in which Philosophy, not a new scripture, argues with the prisoner.

volumes.author: Ignatius Donnelly
volumes.note: A nineteenth-century argument that Atlantis was a real global source. It is a later claim, not Plato.

volumes.author: Edgar Cayce
volumes.note: The trance readings associated with Edgar Cayce, including his Atlantis material. They are modern readings, and the words stay with their rights holders.

volumes.author: attributed to Hermes Trismegistus
volumes.note: A Latin dialogue preserved under Apuleius's name addressing divine creation and Egyptian prophecy.

volumes.author: Nehuniah ben ha-Kanah (attributed)
volumes.note: An early classical Kabbalistic text establishing the doctrine of the ten divine emanations.

volumes.author: attributed to Eleazar of Worms
volumes.note: A practical medieval Kabbalistic grimoire framing celestial hierarchies and esoteric names.

volumes.volume: On the Mysteries of the Egyptians, Chaldeans, and Assyrians
volumes.author: Iamblichus
volumes.note: A late antique philosophical defense of ritual theurgy against Porphyry's rationalist skepticism.

volumes.author: Proclus
volumes.note: A systematic geometric exposition of Neoplatonic metaphysics deriving all multiplicity from the One.

volumes.author: Helena Blavatsky
volumes.note: A foundational Theosophical treatise whose accounts of lost continents and root races remain later claims, not Plato.

volumes.author: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa
volumes.note: A comprehensive Renaissance synthesis unifying natural, celestial, and ceremonial occult philosophy.

volumes.author: Moses ben Jacob Cordovero
volumes.note: A systematic sixteenth-century theological reconciliation of early Kabbalistic traditions and the Zohar.

volumes.author: James Churchward
volumes.note: An assertion of a submerged motherland that stands as a twentieth-century claim, not Plato or ancient history.
